name: Nha Trang Beach
kicker: The city sand along Trần Phú
summary: The city sand runs along Trần Phú. Vietnam Tourism calls this stretch seven kilometres. A beach ticket was not printed, and neither were swim hours. Check on arrival. Vietnam Tourism and the tourism bureau put the drier months in January to August. After dark the same shore is the walk, and the night market sits behind 46 Trần Phú.

body: This is the beach the city is for. Vietnam Tourism treats Nha Trang Beach as the day on the sand and calls Trần Phú a seven-kilometre beach. Hotels face that shore. The evening walk is the same sand, not a second beach.

Vietnam Tourism and the tourism bureau both call January to August the dry season and September to December the rainy season. The tourism bureau prints an average of 26°C. A rescuer’s duty clock was not printed. Chair hire was not printed.

The night market is not on the towel. It is the 137 m walking street behind the cultural centre at 46 Trần Phú, in Lộc Thọ. The provincial digital guide says entry is free. A closing hour was not printed.

gettingThere: The sand is Trần Phú. From a hotel on that road you walk out. From Cam Ranh, the AIP says 27 km from the centre, the city lying to the north, and Vietnam Tourism says about 30 km south. The minutes were not printed. Shuttles, taxis, and ride-hailing are the modes Vietnam Tourism names.
